children: has officially started high-volume production of its long-delayed Semi truck at a new Nevada factory, marking an important step in the company's push beyond passenger vehicles and into commercial trucking.

CEO Elon Musk said production is underway at Tesla's dedicated Semi facility in Sparks, Nevada, which was inaugurated on September 24. The plant is ultimately expected to produce as many as 50,000 trucks annually, although Tesla has not disclosed its current production rate.
The launch has been years in the making.

Tesla first unveiled the Semi in 2017 and began limited deliveries in 2022, but plans for a broader ramp were repeatedly delayed. The long-range version is rated for up to 500 miles on a full charge while carrying a full load, while the standard-range version offers 325 miles.
Early demand is beginning to take shape.

Tesla recently received orders for 2,500 Semis from major cargo-shipping companies, including Microsoft and PepsiCo, according to Catalyst Mobility. Swedish freight technology company Einride separately ordered another 500 trucks. PepsiCo, one of Tesla's earliest customers, already operates Semis, while DHL and US Foods are also among customers.
Musk said the Semi already has a pretty significant waiting list.

Tesla is also pitching lower operating costs as a major selling point, arguing that electricity costs less per mile than diesel. The company eventually plans to integrate autonomous-driving technology into the truck as well.
For Tesla investors, the bigger question is whether the Semi can move from a long-running side project into a meaningful commercial-vehicle business.
The 50,000-unit annual target provides scale, but execution now matters more than promises.
Investors should watch the actual production ramp, delivery volumes, fleet pricing, margins and whether large corporate orders convert into repeat business.

Tesla shares are down nearly 16% year to date, while the average analyst price target of $388.85 implies roughly 2.9% upside. That leaves the Semi ramp as a potentially important new proof point for a stock still looking for stronger operational catalysts.

title: Elon Musk Pushes Tesla Semi Into Its Biggest Phase Yet
